description: #341: a thin CLI bridge that calls .mcp.json servers headlessly and returns a real process exit code + JSON on stdout, so gh->MCP fallback branches become ordinary subprocesses that bkit's bash `|| Failure Path` gates and poll loops handle unmodified, and `0 results` vs `call failed` become distinct exit codes (the live search_issues silent-zero class). Acknowledged as the best long-term shape; deferred because it is a bespoke CLI duplicating the MCP client's auth/session semantics with its own token-scoping + injection surface, and is the new-tooling investment #341's minimal/additive principle rules out
remediation: revisit if the prose fallback (bounded + recorded + re-asserted, per design D13) proves insufficient in practice, or if the fallback path needs to be regression-tested outside a live agent session

description: #341: make PR-based phase-close the single close path in all three runtimes and delete the local squash-merge, so mode 1 (99% of runs) exercises the same close code as mode 3 instead of letting the cloud path rot between uses — the aetiology of D1. Rejected for now: regresses mode 1 (design close is offline + instant today, would need network + PR + CI), collides with the [skip ci] PR-title assert at 5 PRs/feature, and hard-depends on branch-protection settings invisible to git
remediation: revisit if the two-transport asymmetry produces a second D1-class incident; prerequisite is resolving [skip ci] on phase-close subjects (issue 341 section 6d)

description: #341: mcp__github__search_issues silently returns total_count 0 for every query on a PRIVATE repo (control query included) while gh returns 39 — MCP up but returning a benign-looking wrong result on the one surface (trackers, section 6i) that has no fallback by design. Design D12 mitigates the symptom within MCP (a 0 is inconclusive; corroborate via a second MCP list_* signal or report unavailable) because bkit doctrine forbids gh for GitHub/Linear tracker ops. Whether section 6i should admit a narrow read-only gh corroboration probe on private repos is left open
remediation: revisit if MCP-internal corroboration proves unreliable; also needs the root cause diagnosed (bkit-side scope/config vs upstream MCP bug) — currently unknown

summary: TEST_VERDICT / TEST_SCOPE pass via jq --arg and accept empty silently — the counters' --argjson hard-stop has no equivalent
description: #58 explicitly out of scope. The same status-write blocks that pass the counter via --argjson (which hard-fails on an empty value: 'invalid JSON text passed to --argjson', exit 2) pass TEST_VERDICT / TEST_SCOPE via --arg, which accepts empty silently — an unsubstituted verdict writes verdict:"" into status.jsonl rather than failing the step. These are legitimately model judgments and #58 keeps verdict interpretation in the orchestrator, so this is not a counter problem; it is the same substitution assumption with a quieter failure mode. Affected sites include bkit-build.md:538/:612/:936, bkit-debug.md:400/:643/:756, bkit-ship.md:562/:625/:685.
remediation: Validate the verdict against the PASS|FAIL|CONCERNS vocabulary inside the write block (case "$V" in PASS|FAIL|CONCERNS) ;; *) exit 2 ;; esac) so an unsubstituted verdict routes to the Failure Path instead of writing an empty string into the log; or move the verdict through --argjson with an enum-validating jq filter.

summary: PRIOR_STRATEGY folds status.jsonl with ALL-runs scoping; whether a resumed run should restart the STANDARD->PIVOT->FINAL ladder was never established
description: #58 flagged but did not change this. PRIOR_STRATEGY (bkit-build.md:592 and :987, bkit-debug.md:624, bkit-ship.md:665) reads [.[] | .steps[] | select(...)] | last.strategy — .[] spans ALL runs. Verified: given a completed run that recorded PIVOT and a fresh second run with no diagnose rows of its own, the shipped read returns PIVOT; an active-run-scoped read returns empty. #58 scopes its attempt derivation to the ACTIVE run — deliberately OPPOSITE — because cross-run counting would hand a resumed workflow the previous run's attempts and starve its budget immediately (the starvation DE-25 had to fix for SOAK). Both sites now carry a comment naming the asymmetry, since it looks like a bug from either direction. What strategy actually wants was not established: a resumed run arguably should NOT restart the ladder from scratch, which would make the all-runs read correct.
remediation: Decide the intended resume semantics for strategy, then either scope the read to the active run (matching the attempt derivation) or record the cross-run behaviour as intentional in .bkit/workflows.md § Status so the asymmetry stops reading as an oversight.

summary: No CI gate runs shellcheck over .bkit/scripts/*.sh — actionlint only shellchecks run: blocks inside .github/workflows/*
description: Discovered while planning #58. The shipped shell surface (.bkit/scripts/bkit-counter-bus.sh, bkit-counter-bus-config.sh, bkit-slop-delta.sh, bkit-protect-main.sh, bkit-set-dependabot.sh, and #58's new bkit-status-fold.sh) is sourced by consumers under sh/dash/zsh but is linted by nothing: the bkit-tests-static lane runs actionlint, which shellchecks only the run: blocks inside .github/workflows/*. The SC2016 disable #58 adds to bkit-status-fold.sh (the fold blob's $w/$e/$i are jq variables, not shell) is therefore defensive for local runs only. A real POSIX-portability regression in a shipped script would land green and only surface in a consumer's shell.
remediation: Add a shellcheck -s sh step over .bkit/scripts/*.sh to the bkit-tests-static lane (and the .bkit/templates/.bkit/scripts/*.sh sources). Scope to the shipped scripts, not the whole repo, and pin the shellcheck version the way actionlint is pinned.

summary: The 'start a new run?' test keys on the last run overall, not the last run of THIS workflow — an interleaved debug run can silently reset a resuming build's attempt budget
description: Surfaced by plan review of #58. bkit-build.md:335 tests (.[-1] // {}) — the last folded run of ANY workflow — to decide whether to append a fresh workflow-started row. build and debug write to the SAME docs/plans/{YYYYMM}/logs/{FID}/status.jsonl. So if a debug run interleaves and completes between two build invocations, a resuming build sees .[-1].workflow == 'debug', appends a fresh workflow-started, and starts a NEW active run — resetting its attempt budget. #58 makes active-run scoping the basis of every counter, which promotes this from latent to load-bearing: it is Defect 3 (fresh budget on resume) through a side door, reachable via the exact build->debug->build path the feature governs. A lock exists at bkit-build.md:143; whether it excludes the interleave is NOT established. #58 characterises current behaviour in tests/counter-derive.bats (T2.10) so the dependence is visible rather than latent, but does not change the boundary.
remediation: Decide the intended run-boundary semantics and key the test on the last run OF THE SAME WORKFLOW (e.g. [.[] | select(.workflow==$w)] | last) rather than .[-1], or establish and document that the bkit-build.md:143 lock makes the interleave impossible. Belongs with #209's status.jsonl substrate, not with #58's control-flow slice. Read T2.10's characterisation assertion first — it records what today actually does.

summary: debug-run-tests writes its step-done row with no commit (KN-26 removed it), so NORMAL_ATTEMPT's row counting depends transitively on Steps 4/5/6 advancing parentSha
description: Surfaced by plan review of #58. #58 counts step-done rows and dedups on 'S {workflow} {step} {parentSha} {at}'. build-run-tests commits --allow-empty per attempt (bkit-build.md:939), so its parentSha advances by itself. debug-run-tests does NOT (bkit-debug.md:396 reads 'Update status:' with no commit — the only step-done-writing step in debug without one). That asymmetry is KN-26's remediation: a chore(...) commit as branch HEAD makes the Vercel-ignore regex skip the preview, CI demotes to partial, integration/Playwright are skipped, and the run reports conclusion=success with no coverage. So NORMAL_ATTEMPT's attempts stay distinct only via Steps 4/5/6's commits (bkit-debug.md:573/:646/:707) advancing parentSha, plus the dedup key's 'at' second. Whether debug-run-tests SHOULD regain a commit — making its row counting self-sufficient — is a real design question that collides with KN-26 and must not be settled by an implementer applying #58's per-site shape. #58 pins the current shape with a corpus audit (T2.6) that requires each counted step to either commit in-block or sit on a commented transitive-exemption list.
remediation: If debug-run-tests's transitive parentSha dependency proves fragile, resolve it WITHOUT re-adding a chore(...) commit — e.g. amend the dedup key, or have the step commit under a subject the Vercel-ignore regex does not match. Any change must be reviewed against KN-26's full failure chain first. Do not simply delete the T2.6 exemption entry.

summary: The 5 close-workflow counter emitters declare counterName DESIGN_ATTEMPT/PLAN_ATTEMPT/BUILD_ATTEMPT/... but #58 derives counterValue from the workflow-started count — the pairing is unverified
description: Surfaced by plan review of #58. #58's T7.1 replaces --argjson counterValue 1 (a hardcoded literal labelled model-self-report) with a fold-derived all-runs count of workflow-started events for that workflow, and flips counterSource to shell-bus. That makes the VALUE honest — it is a real number the shell counted. Whether that number is what each emitter's declared counterName means is a separate question #58 does not adjudicate: the names (DESIGN_ATTEMPT, PLAN_ATTEMPT, BUILD_ATTEMPT, ...) suggest an invocation index, which the workflow-started count is, but this was asserted rather than established against #234's schema intent. Flagged so the value/name pairing is not quietly assumed correct by the next reader of stats.jsonl.
remediation: Settle alongside #234's counterSource enum question ('derived' vs 'shell-bus' — which names the transport rather than the provenance). Confirm each emitter's counterName denotes an invocation index; if any denotes something else, either rename it or derive a different value for that emitter. #234 owns the schema.

summary: periodic bkit-analysis pass summarising transport-fallback frequency against GH_OK=false runs
description: #341 OQ5 (design, recorded not-adopted): a recurring reader that aggregates status.jsonl transport-fallback rows against runtime-resolved GH_OK=false runs to surface how often the gh->MCP fallback fires in mode 3. Out of scope for #341 — it is a new analysis feature, not part of the runtime-execution change. Design D25 already gives the rows a mechanical reader inside the Close Workflow (the part that belongs to #341); the aggregation/reporting layer is the additive extra.
remediation: revisit if transport-fallback frequency becomes an operational concern post-ship; a new bkit-analysis reader over the existing status.jsonl rows, no new artifact type

summary: mode-tuned concurrency pacing for subagent fan-out vs the shared-account rate budget on the claude.ai runner
description: #341 §6g (N2, deferred): the claude.ai runner shares an account-level rate budget, so a phase's subagent fan-out can hit shared-account rate limits that modes 1/2 do not. Deferred in the issue as 'revisit only if hit'; the fix would be mode-tuned concurrency pacing (throttle fan-out when RUNTIME=3). Out of scope for #341's minimal/additive runtime-execution change.
remediation: revisit only if a live mode-3 run (WS-16) actually hits the shared-account rate ceiling; fix would pace fan-out concurrency on RUNTIME=3
